title: What is the difference between .NET Framework, .NET Core, and .NET 6/7/8?
description: Understand the evolution of .NET platforms and when to use each.

data.text: **Question:** What is the difference between .NET Framework, .NET Core, and .NET 6/7/8?

.NET Framework is the original Windows-only implementation. .NET Core was a cross-platform rewrite. .NET 6/7/8 unified them into a single platform called just '.NET', which is cross-platform, high-performance, and the future of .NET development.

**.NET Framework:**
- Windows-only
- Released in 2002
- Mature, stable, backward compatible
- Uses CLR and System.Web
- Still supported but no new features

**.NET Core (1.0-3.1):**
- Cross-platform (Windows, Linux, macOS)
- Open source, modular
- High performance
- Unified MVC and Web API
- Short support lifecycle

**.NET 5/6/7/8 (modern .NET):**
- Unified platform replacing both Framework and Core
- Long-term support (LTS) releases: .NET 6, .NET 8
- Cross-platform by default
- Single BCL (Base Class Library)
- Better performance with each release
